lines.text: The writer tells his son to continue always in the fear of the LORD and not envy sinners.
The drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and the son should listen to his father.
The writer says to invest in truth and never sell it, and calls an adulteress a narrow well.
Those who linger over wine suffer woe, and in the end it bites like a lion.
The drinker will see strange things, be like one lying on top of a cedar, and seek another drink.
